subtopicTitle: Derivation of Euler-Lagrange equations from D'Alembert's principle

cards.front: State D'Alembert's principle for a system of N particles.
cards.back: $$\sum_{i=1}^N (\mathbf{F}_i - m_i \ddot{\mathbf{r}}_i) \cdot \delta \mathbf{r}_i = 0$$ where $\delta \mathbf{r}_i$ are virtual displacements consistent with instantaneous constraints.

cards.front: Express virtual displacement $\delta \mathbf{r}_i$ in generalized coordinates $q_j$.
Define the generalized force $Q_j$ from applied forces.
For conservative forces derive $Q_j = -\partial V/\partial q_j$.
cards.back: Since $\mathbf{F}_i = -\nabla_i V$, substitute to obtain $Q_j = -\sum_i \nabla_i V \cdot \partial \mathbf{r}_i / \partial q_j = -\partial V / \partial q_j$.

cards.front: Show that $\sum_i m_i \ddot{\mathbf{r}}_i \cdot \partial \mathbf{r}_i / \partial q_j = d/dt(\partial T/\partial \dot q_j) - \partial T/\partial q_j$.
cards.back: Start from $T=\frac12\sum m_i \dot{\mathbf{r}}_i^2$, differentiate w.r.t. $q_j$ and $\dot q_j$, apply chain rule and product rule; the left-hand side equals the right-hand side after rearrangement.

cards.front: Write the intermediate equation before introducing the Lagrangian.
cards.back: $$\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{\partial T}{\partial \dot q_j}\right) - \frac{\partial T}{\partial q_j} = Q_j$$ for each independent $j$.

cards.front: Obtain the Euler-Lagrange equation by substituting $Q_j=-\partial V/\partial q_j$.
cards.back: Define $L=T-V$. Then $$\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{\partial L}{\partial \dot q_j}\right) - \frac{\partial L}{\partial q_j}=0$$.

cards.front: State the final Euler-Lagrange equations derived from D'Alembert's principle.
cards.back: For each $j=1\dots n$: $$\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{\partial L}{\partial \dot q_j}\right) - \frac{\partial L}{\partial q_j}=0$$ where $L(q,\dot q,t)=T-V$.
